facts.fact: Agentforce Builder is the in-org agent builder located inside Agentforce Studio in the App Launcher, and admin permissions control access (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/script/).

The new Agentforce Builder is GA and available to all customers and in Developer Edition orgs, but secondary sources disagree on the release: one says GA in February 2026 (Spring '26), another Summer '26 (secondary) (https://admin.salesforce.com/?p=194943).

A secondary news site says that from the week of 2026-07-13 the Setup New Agent button no longer opens the legacy Agentforce builder, while existing legacy agents keep running (secondary) (https://salesforcedictionary.com/news/salesforce-news-july-12-2026-agentforce-legacy-builder-retires).

The new Agentforce Builder reportedly replaces the legacy builder from the week of 2026-07-13 (secondary) (https://salesforcedictionary.com/news/salesforce-news-july-12-2026-agentforce-legacy-builder-retires).

Agent Script is the language behind Agentforce Builder, mixing deterministic rules (subagent transitions, action sequencing) with LLM reasoning, and is included with Agentforce at no extra cost (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/script/).
Agentforce Builder's Canvas view and Script view both edit Agent Script (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-script.html).
Agentforce DX and Agent Script went GA in Salesforce CLI on 2026-02-18, after a beta that started 2025-12-10 (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Agentforce DX is delivered in Salesforce CLI (GA 2026-02-18) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

Agents are stored as the `AiAuthoringBundle` metadata type (an `.agent` Agent Script file plus `bundle-meta.xml`) under `force-app/main/default/aiAuthoringBundles/` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
CLI release 2.133.4 (2026-05-06) says As of April 2026, agent `topics` in Agent Script files are now called `subagents` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
The Agent Script compiler moved to v2.0.0, which is backward compatible (https://www.salesforce.com/blog/connect-agentforce-external-mcp-servers/).

`sf agent publish authoring-bundle` compiles an `AiAuthoringBundle` and creates `Bot`, `BotVersion`, `GenAiPlannerBundle` and `GenAiPlugin` metadata, i.e. the runtime agent (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-generate/references/agent-metadata-and-lifecycle.md).

`sf project deploy start` only stages the `AiAuthoringBundle` as a DRAFT in Builder and does not create the runtime agent; publishing does (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-generate/references/agent-metadata-and-lifecycle.md).

Service agents run as a dedicated Einstein Agent User set in the Agent Script `config` block with `default_agent_user` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-generate/references/agent-user-setup.md).
`sf org create agent-user` (added 2026-04-01) creates the Einstein Agent User that a service agent runs as (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

Agent actions can be Apex invocable actions, Flows, prompt templates and external services (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-generate/references/agent-metadata-and-lifecycle.md).

At deploy time every action target (Apex class, Flow, Prompt Template) must resolve to a registered invocable action in the org, or the deploy fails (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-generate/references/agent-metadata-and-lifecycle.md).

Atlas Reasoning Engine is the name Salesforce uses for Agentforce's reasoning layer, but no current official page defining it could be fetched and the Agent Script page does not mention it (unverified) (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/script/).

Agentforce Testing Center runs batch tests defined as `AiEvaluationDefinition` metadata, created and run with `sf agent test create` and `sf agent test run` (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-agent).
Salesforce advises running Agentforce Testing Center only in sandboxes (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-test/SKILL.md).

`sf agent test run-eval` (beta, added 2026-05-20) runs evaluation tests with a state-based evaluation framework, at most 5 tests per API request (`--batch-size`), with output as `json`, `human`, `junit` or `tap` (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-agent).

facts.fact: Agent observability comes from Session Trace Data Model (STDM) records in Data 360, which require the Agentforce Activity data stream (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-observe/SKILL.md).
Agentforce session tracing data can also be exported via OpenTelemetry (beta) (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/otel-api.html).
`sf agent trace list|read|delete` (added 2026-05-20) manage the trace files recorded by local agent preview (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
The Agentforce DX VS Code extension shows local agent preview trace data in an Agent Tracer tab (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

Agentforce Data Libraries (ADL) are the retrieval/RAG grounding source, with library source type `sfdrive` (uploaded files, basic or enhanced index), `knowledge` (Knowledge articles) or `retriever` (an existing Data 360 retriever) (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-agent).
`sf agent adl` commands manage Agentforce Data Libraries (developer preview since 2026-06-10) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Salesforce's product page reads Data 360 (Formerly Data Cloud); no rename date is given there (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Data 360's named grounding and memory features are Agent Context Engine (ACE), Persistent Agent Memory and Trusted Grounding (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Persistent Agent Memory is a Data 360 feature (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Trusted Grounding is a Data 360 feature (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Data 360 zero-copy connects to Snowflake, Databricks (Delta Sharing), Google BigQuery and AWS (S3, Redshift) (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Data 360 zero-copy connects to Databricks through Delta Sharing (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Data 360 zero-copy connects to Google BigQuery (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Data 360 zero-copy connects to AWS S3 and Redshift (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).

The Salesforce Models API serves LLMs at `https://api.salesforce.com/ai/gpt/v1` with fully qualified model aliases (`sfdc_ai__...`) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/platform-models-api-configure/SKILL.md).

The Models API needs an OrgJWT from a connected app with the `sfap_api` OAuth scope and the `client_credentials` flow (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/platform-models-api-configure/SKILL.md).
An unsigned `sf org display` session token returns 404 from the Models API (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/platform-models-api-configure/SKILL.md).

Trailhead says Agentforce applies the Einstein Trust Layer and a zero data retention policy to MCP tools; the Trust Layer product page URL tried (`/agentforce/einstein-trust-layer/`) returned 404 (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/mcp-for-agentforce-quick-look/discover-mcp-for-agentforce).

Prompt Builder templates can be agent actions and hosted-MCP custom tools, and prompt templates deploy as metadata (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-generate/references/agent-metadata-and-lifecycle.md).
Einstein Copilot became Agentforce; exact rename dates were not confirmed (unverified) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills).

Agentforce for Developers is now Agentforce Vibes, the name used for the IDE assistant in CLI release notes and the `forcedotcom/sf-skills` README; exact rename dates were not confirmed (unverified) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills).
Salesforce docs host Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers in Agentforce Vibes under the `einstein-for-devs` path (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/einstein-for-devs/guide/hostedmcp.html).

Agentforce 360 was announced GA as the unified agentic AI platform name (secondary) (https://sdtimes.com/ai/salesforce-announces-general-availability-of-its-unified-agentic-ai-platform-agentforce-360/).
MuleSoft Agent Fabric is GA (https://www.mulesoft.com/ai/agent-fabric).

MuleSoft Agent Fabric components are Agent Registry, Agent Broker (multi-agent orchestration), Agent Visualizer, Agent Governance (Unified LLM and MCP Gateway, Agent Evals, Trusted Agent Identity, Agent Kill Switch, AI cost controls), Scanners and MCP Bridge; the page does not mention Topic Center (https://www.mulesoft.com/ai/agent-fabric).

Heroku Managed Inference and Agents (add-on `heroku-inference`) offers an agent endpoint `POST $INFERENCE_URL/v1/agents/heroku` with tool execution, where tools run in isolated one-off dynos (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-inference-working-with-mcp).
No Salesforce-native agent computer-use or browser-use product was found (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/script/).

Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers have been GA since 2026-04-29 for Enterprise Edition and above, following a pilot in spring 2025 and a beta in October 2025, and Developer Edition orgs can also use them (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2026/04/salesforce-hosted-mcp-servers-are-now-generally-available).
Docs say hosted MCP servers are intended for orgs with Flex Credits and usage may be billed (https://www.scalekit.com/blog/salesforce-mcp-server (secondary)).

Hosted MCP endpoints follow `https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/<path>`, with production at `.../v1/platform/<server>` and sandbox or scratch orgs at `.../v1/sandbox/platform/<server>`; the beta URL pattern `mcp/v1-beta.2` was retired at GA (secondary) (https://www.speakeasy.com/docs/ai-control-plane/guides/salesforce.md).

facts.fact: Standard hosted MCP servers are `sobject-reads` (query, search and relationship traversal, no writes), `sobject-mutations` (create and update, no delete), `sobject-deletes` (delete only), `sobject-all` (full CRUD plus query and search), `data360`, `headless-360` and `analytics/tableau-next` (secondary) (https://www.speakeasy.com/docs/ai-control-plane/guides/salesforce.md).
The `data360` hosted MCP server at `.../v1/data/data360` needs a Data 360 license and API v66.0+ (secondary) (https://www.speakeasy.com/docs/ai-control-plane/guides/salesforce.md).
The `headless-360` hosted MCP server is Beta from July 2026, covers broad Setup operations and needs API v67.0+ (secondary) (https://www.speakeasy.com/docs/ai-control-plane/guides/salesforce.md).

Hosted MCP auth requires an External Client App, not a classic Connected App, with OAuth scopes `mcp_api` and `refresh_token`; the standard `api` scope does not work (secondary) (https://www.librechat.ai/docs/mcp_servers/salesforce).
Hosted MCP tool calls run as the signed-in user, subject to field-level security, object permissions and sharing (secondary) (https://www.speakeasy.com/docs/ai-control-plane/guides/salesforce.md).

Hosted MCP servers are off by default; an admin activates them in Setup > API Catalog > MCP Servers, activation takes up to 2 minutes, and a new External Client App can take up to 30 minutes to work (secondary) (https://www.speakeasy.com/docs/ai-control-plane/guides/salesforce.md).

Custom hosted MCP servers can publish org logic as tools from Flows, Apex invocable actions, `@AuraEnabled` methods, Apex REST endpoints, API Catalog APIs and Prompt Builder templates, while standard server tools cannot be modified (secondary) (https://www.librechat.ai/docs/mcp_servers/salesforce).

The local Salesforce DX MCP Server (`@salesforce/mcp`) reached end of life on 2026-11-02; the last version is 0.30.15 (published 2026-07-09) and the repo `salesforcecli/mcp` is archived (https://github.com/forcedotcom/mcp/issues/46).
The Salesforce DX MCP Server ran via `npx -y @salesforce/mcp --orgs <alias> --toolsets <...>` using local `sf` CLI auth (https://registry.npmjs.org/@salesforce/mcp).
After the local DX MCP Server's end of life, Salesforce delivers tooling as skills in `forcedotcom/sf-skills` (https://github.com/salesforcecli/mcp).
`forcedotcom/sf-skills` is Salesforce's official skills collection; install standalone skills with `npx skills add forcedotcom/sf-skills` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills).

The Salesforce Development plugin's `.mcp.json` wires stdio proxies to hosted `metadata-experts`, `metadata-grounding` and opt-in `headless-360` MCP servers (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/plugins/builder/salesforce-development/.mcp.json).
`forcedotcom/sf-skills` includes a Salesforce Development plugin for Claude Code and Codex (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills).
The Salesforce Development plugin is available for Codex (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills).
Agentforce has a native MCP client for calling external MCP servers (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/mcp-for-agentforce-quick-look/discover-mcp-for-agentforce).

Admins register external MCP servers in Setup's Agentforce Registry and choose which discovered tools to allow, then builders assign tools per subagent in Agentforce Builder (https://www.salesforce.com/blog/connect-agentforce-external-mcp-servers/).

Supported auth for external MCP servers in Agentforce is OAuth 2.0, external (named) credentials or none (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/mcp-for-agentforce-quick-look/discover-mcp-for-agentforce).

External MCP OAuth options are per-user OAuth (`authorization_code` grant, named credential plus external credential with a Per-User Principal) or a service account (`client_credentials` grant), and Salesforce warns that service-account access is all-or-nothing (2026-07-28) (https://www.salesforce.com/blog/connect-agentforce-external-mcp-servers/).

Secondary sources say the Agentforce MCP client was pilot in July 2025 and beta in January 2026; no official GA date was found (secondary) (https://vantagepoint.io/blog/sf/agentforce-mcp-connect-external-systems-guide).

Agentforce Gateway sets MCP usage policies per agent and tool, such as call-rate caps (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/mcp-for-agentforce-quick-look/discover-mcp-for-agentforce).

`sf agent mcp create|list|get|update|delete|fetch` and `sf agent mcp asset list|replace` register external MCP servers in API Catalog (developer preview since 2026-07-08); `create` takes `--server-url` and `--auth-type OAUTH|NO_AUTH` with `--identity-provider`, `--client-id`, `--client-secret` and `--scope` (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-agent).
Salesforce CLI `sf agent mcp` commands register external MCP servers in API Catalog (developer preview since 2026-07-08) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
The Slackbot MCP client is GA, with more than 20 partner apps live (https://www.salesforce.com/blog/connect-agentforce-external-mcp-servers/).

The Slackbot MCP client is read-only by default with per-action user confirmation for writes and deletes, access control is app-level only, and Slack apps declare the `mcp:connect` scope (https://www.salesforce.com/blog/connect-agentforce-external-mcp-servers/).
The Slack MCP server is at `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp` using Streamable HTTP and JSON-RPC 2.0 (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/mcp-server).
The Slack MCP server does not support SSE or Dynamic Client Registration and needs confidential OAuth from a registered directory-published or internal app (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/mcp-server).
Slack MCP server tools cover search, messages, canvases, users, files and lists at per-tool Web API rate tiers (Tier 2 20+/min to Tier 4 100+/min) (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/mcp-server).

facts.fact: The Slack Real-time Search (RTS) API gives direct search over Slack data without an AI client in the loop (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/mcp-server).

Agentforce Agent API (headless agents) is REST under `https://api.salesforce.com/einstein/ai-agent/v1`, with Government Cloud using `api.gov.salesforce.com` (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-api-get-started.html).

Agent API endpoints are `POST /agents/{AGENT_ID}/sessions` to start a session, `/sessions/{sessionId}/messages` to send a message synchronously, `/sessions/{sessionId}/messages/stream` to stream (an `EndOfTurn` event marks the end), and `/sessions/{sessionId}` to end the session (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agent-api-quick-look/build-custom-ai-agents-with-agent-api).

Agent API auth uses an External Client App with the client credentials flow, minting the Bearer token from the consumer key and secret plus the My Domain (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agent-api-quick-look/build-custom-ai-agents-with-agent-api).
Agent API calls authenticate through an External Client App (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agent-api-quick-look/build-custom-ai-agents-with-agent-api).

The Agent API session body takes `externalSessionKey`, `instanceConfig.endpoint` and `streamingCapabilities.chunkTypes` (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agent-api-quick-look/build-custom-ai-agents-with-agent-api).
Agent API calls consume credits (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agent-api-quick-look/build-custom-ai-agents-with-agent-api).

Salesforce contributed the Agent Card concept to the A2A protocol, but no official Agentforce A2A doc was fetched; one secondary source says Winter '27 markets Agentforce third-party orchestration across A2A-compliant ecosystems and another (April 2026 guidance) calls Agentforce MCP and A2A support beta (secondary) (https://www.salesforce.com/blog/agent-interoperability/).

MuleSoft Agent Fabric A2A Support uses pre-built connectors to make agents A2A-compliant, and its Agent Registry lists public MCP servers from the Official MCP Registry (https://www.mulesoft.com/ai/agent-fabric).
MuleSoft MCP Connector 1.7 makes Mule apps MCP servers or MCP clients, with Streamable HTTP the recommended transport (https://docs.mulesoft.com/mcp-connector/latest/).
In MuleSoft MCP Connector, SSE is deprecated and the SSE server transport works only in single-replica deployments (https://docs.mulesoft.com/mcp-connector/latest/).
Heroku AppLink is the new name of Heroku Integration (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-applink).

Heroku AppLink publishes Heroku apps to Salesforce as External Services, API Catalog entries and Agentforce actions, callable from Apex, Flow, Data Cloud Data Action Targets and Agentforce, with user modes `user`, `user-plus` and `authorized-user` (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-applink).
Heroku AppLink has Node.js and Python SDKs (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-applink).
The Heroku AppLink service runs in the `virginia` region (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-applink).

Procfile process names starting with `mcp` register with the Managed Inference and Agents add-on, created with `heroku addons:create heroku-inference:standard` (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-inference-working-with-mcp).
External clients reach the Heroku MCP Toolkit at `$INFERENCE_URL/mcp/sse` with Bearer `$INFERENCE_KEY` (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-inference-working-with-mcp).
MCP servers in Heroku Private Spaces cannot be registered with the MCP Toolkit (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-inference-working-with-mcp).
The REST API base URL is `https://MyDomainName.my.salesforce.com/services/data/vXX.X/`, with OAuth Bearer tokens (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_rest.pdf).
The current REST API version is v68.0 (Winter '27) (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_rest.pdf).

A regular composite request allows 25 subrequests, composite graphs allow 500 nodes, and composite batch (`/services/data/vXX.X/composite/batch`) runs up to 25 subrequests (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_rest.pdf).

Bulk API 2.0 suits operations over 2,000 records, uploads go up to 150 MB per job after base64 encoding, and query jobs do automatic PK chunking (v68.0 guide) (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_asynch.pdf).

Pub/Sub API is the recommended event API over the CometD-based Streaming API, handling platform events, Change Data Capture and real-time event monitoring events (https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api).
Pub/Sub API is gRPC over HTTP/2 with Avro payloads at `api.pubsub.salesforce.com:7443` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api).
Streaming API PushTopic and generic events are labelled Legacy (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_streaming.pdf).
GraphQL API is reachable from the CLI with `sf api request graphql --body <file>`, and SOAP API and the Metadata API are also available (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-api).
Salesforce offers SOAP API and the Metadata API alongside REST and GraphQL (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-api).
Salesforce exposes the Metadata API (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-api).

JSforce is the main JavaScript SDK for Salesforce, a community project not owned by Salesforce, published on npm as `jsforce` (latest 3.13.1) and covering REST, Apex REST, Bulk, Metadata, Analytics and Chatter APIs (third-party) (https://registry.npmjs.org/jsforce).
Salesforce CLI depends on the community JSforce library (third-party) (https://github.com/jsforce/jsforce).

facts.fact: simple-salesforce is a third-party Python REST client (PyPI `simple-salesforce`, latest 1.12.10) covering the REST API and Apex REST (third-party) (https://pypi.org/project/simple-salesforce/).
simple-salesforce latest is 1.12.10 and supports Python 3.9 to 3.13 (third-party) (https://github.com/simple-salesforce/simple-salesforce).
Zero-copy connectors link Data 360 to Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and AWS S3/Redshift (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Salesforce CLI (`sf`) v2 is current and `sfdx` v7 gets no updates (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
The latest stable Salesforce CLI is 2.158.7 (2026-11-04) and the release candidate is 2.159.7 (2026-11-11); stable releases ship on Wednesdays (https://registry.npmjs.org/@salesforce/cli).

On Windows, install Salesforce CLI with the `sf-x64.exe` installer from the CLI download page (direct link `https://developer.salesforce.com/media/salesforce-cli/sf/channels/stable/sf-x64.exe`, HTTP 200 on 2026-11-14), which optionally adds `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sf` to Defender exclusions (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_setup.pdf).

Salesforce recommends `cmd.exe` or PowerShell over WSL, cygwin or MinGW for the CLI on Windows, the Windows x86 installer was removed in February 2026, and no winget package was found (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
`npm install @salesforce/cli --global` needs Node.js 22 or later (since 2026-08-12), and the installers bundle Node.js 24 (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Update Salesforce CLI with `sf update stable`, or `npm install @salesforce/cli@latest --global` for npm installs (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

Login options are `sf org login web` (browser web-server flow; supports `--instance-url`, `--client-id`, `--scopes`, and `--client-app` with `--username` to link an external client app), `sf org login jwt` (`--username`, `--jwt-key-file`, `--client-id`, for CI), `sf org login access-token` (an existing access token) and `sf org login sfdx-url` (an SFDX auth URL file) (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-auth).
`sf org login device` was removed on 2026-01-20 because Salesforce blocks the OAuth device flow (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

CLI config and credentials live under `.sf` and `.sfdx` in the user home directory; on Windows the encryption key is in `C:\Users\<username>\.sfdx\key.json`, macOS uses Keychain and Linux uses libsecret unless `SF_USE_GENERIC_UNIX_KEYCHAIN=true` (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_setup.pdf).
Since 2026-10-28 Salesforce CLI always redacts secrets from output; use the `sf org auth show-*` commands to view them (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
The `sf agent` command group comes from `@salesforce/plugin-agent` 2.3.0 (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-agent).

Main `sf agent` subcommands are `generate agent-spec|authoring-bundle|template|test-spec`, `validate authoring-bundle`, `publish authoring-bundle` (supports `--skip-retrieve`), `activate` and `deactivate`, `preview start|send|end|sessions` (`start` takes `--authoring-bundle` with `--simulate-actions` or `--use-live-actions`, or `--api-name`), `test create|run|run-eval|results|resume|list`, `trace list|read|delete`, `adl ...` and `mcp ...` (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-agent).
`@salesforce/plugin-agent` is at version 2.3.0 (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-agent).

Previewing a published agent with `sf agent preview` no longer needs a dedicated connected app: the `--client-app` flag was removed, so a standard `sf org login web` is enough (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

`sf project` handles source deploys: `deploy start|validate|quick|preview|report|resume|cancel`, `retrieve start|preview`, `generate manifest`, `convert source|mdapi|source-behavior`, `reset tracking` and `delete tracking` (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-deploy-retrieve).

`sf api request rest [URL]` and `sf api request graphql` make authenticated calls with the CLI's stored auth (both GA since 2026-08-19); `rest` supports `-X` method, `-H` headers, `-b` body or `@file`, `-f` JSON request file and `-S` stream-to-file (https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-api).

`org create scratch` fails when the Dev Hub uses an external client app with JWT; the workaround (added 2026-08-12) is to set `SF_SCRATCH_SIGNUP_CONNECTED_APP=PlatformCLI` and `SF_SCRATCH_SIGNUP_CALLBACK_URL` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
The Agentforce DX VS Code extension has Marketplace ID `salesforce.salesforcedx-vscode-agents` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
The Agent Script language extension has Marketplace ID `salesforce.agent-script-language-client` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

The developer docs root is `https://developer.salesforce.com/docs`; it returned HTTP 403 to automated clients on 2026-11-14, so it was not verified as reachable by agents (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs).

Agentforce developer docs moved from `/docs/einstein/genai/guide/` to `/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/`, where Agent API, Agent Script and Agentforce DX pages now appear, with old-path copies still indexed; both returned 403 to automated fetch (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-dx.html).

Hosted MCP Servers docs are at `https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/`, with pages including `sobject-all.html`, `products-supporting-mcp.html` and `connection-issues.html` (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers/guide/products-supporting-mcp.html).

Agent-readable PDFs of the developer guides (v68.0, Winter '27) are on `resources.docs.salesforce.com`, for example `.../sfdc/pdf/api_rest.pdf`, `api_asynch.pdf`, `api_streaming.pdf`, `salesforce_apex_developer_guide.pdf`, `sfdx_setup.pdf` and `salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf` (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

`https://developer.salesforce.com/llms.txt` returned 403 so its existence is unconfirmed, and no official docs MCP server was found (unverified) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/platform-docs-get/SKILL.md).

The official `platform-docs-get` skill in `forcedotcom/sf-skills` is Salesforce's own documented way to fetch JS-heavy Salesforce docs (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/platform-docs-get/SKILL.md).

CLI release notes are in the `forcedotcom/cli` GitHub repo, the command reference is at `developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/`, and each plugin README (for example `salesforcecli/plugin-agent`) documents its flags (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Help and release notes are at `https://help.salesforce.com/s/` (HTTP 200), but articles need a JavaScript-rendering fetcher (https://help.salesforce.com/s/).
The status page is `https://status.salesforce.com/` (HTTP 200), with Heroku status under `/products/Heroku` (https://status.salesforce.com/).

Official sample repos are `forcedotcom/sf-skills` (skills and plugins), `forcedotcom/pub-sub-api` (Pub/Sub clients) and the Heroku MCP starters `heroku/mcp-code-exec-python` and `heroku/mcp-doc-reader` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api).
Slack developer docs are at `https://docs.slack.dev/` (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/mcp-server).
MuleSoft docs are at `https://docs.mulesoft.com/` (https://docs.mulesoft.com/mcp-connector/latest/).
Heroku docs are at `https://devcenter.heroku.com/` (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-applink).

Concurrent API requests lasting 20 seconds or longer are limited to 25 at a time in production orgs and sandboxes and 5 in Developer Edition and trial orgs; excess calls fail with `REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, while requests shorter than 20 seconds have no concurrency limit (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

Enterprise and Professional (with API access) orgs get 100,000 API calls per 24 hours plus 1,000 per Salesforce or Salesforce Platform license plus purchased add-ons, Developer Edition gets 15,000, and paid orgs can overrun temporarily up to a hard cap (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

REST and SOAP calls time out after 10 minutes, query calls follow SOQL limits, and for Composite the timeout covers the whole request (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

facts.fact: Bulk API and Bulk API 2.0 share 15,000 batches per rolling 24 hours, and in Bulk API 2.0 only ingest jobs consume batches (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

Bulk API 2.0 shares a 15,000 batches per rolling 24 hours allocation with Bulk API, consumed only by ingest jobs (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

Apex governor limits per transaction (sync/async) per Apex Developer Guide v68.0 (Winter '27): SOQL queries 100/200, rows retrieved by SOQL 50,000, DML statements 150, rows processed by DML 10,000, callouts 100 with 120 seconds cumulative callout timeout, heap 10 MB/25 MB, and CPU time 10,000 ms/60,000 ms (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_apex_developer_guide.pdf).
The Apex heap limit is printed as 10 MB/25 MB in v68.0, while older docs said 6 MB/12 MB (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_apex_developer_guide.pdf).
Agent API calls time out after 120 seconds and return HTTP 500 (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agent-api-quick-look/build-custom-ai-agents-with-agent-api).

The Agent API does not support agents of type Agentforce (Default), and sessions should be closed when finished (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agent-api-quick-look/build-custom-ai-agents-with-agent-api).

Secondary sources cite 20 active agents per org, 15 topics (subagents) per agent and 15 actions per topic, and say actions should finish in about 60 seconds and run under normal Apex governor limits (secondary) (https://atrium.ai/resources/agentforce-limitations-developer-workarounds/).

For hosted MCP, classic Connected Apps and the `api` scope fail; use an External Client App with `mcp_api` and `refresh_token`, and a new app can take up to 30 minutes to work (secondary) (https://www.librechat.ai/docs/mcp_servers/salesforce).

A secondary source says Agentforce cannot complete a browser redirect when registering an external MCP server, so client credentials is the usual route, and Trailblazer threads report We couldn't connect to the MCP server errors (secondary) (https://neo4j.com/labs/genai-ecosystem/genai-frameworks/salesforce-agentforce-mcp/).

For Agent Script bundles, `sf project deploy start` does not create runtime agents (use `sf agent publish authoring-bundle`), version-suffixed bundles retrieved after publish carry a `<target>` lock so edited deploys of them fail, and a bare `sf project deploy start` also deploys changed agent metadata, so scope it with `--metadata` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills/blob/main/skills/agentforce-generate/references/agent-metadata-and-lifecycle.md).

`sf agent preview start --authoring-bundle` requires `--simulate-actions` or `--use-live-actions` (change in 2026); it used to default to simulated actions (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

For Heroku AppLink, admins must allowlist AppLink IPs in the org, AppLink works only with editions that have API access, and latency depends on distance from Virginia (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-applink).
Slack MCP rate limits match the Web API tiers, and app IP allowlists also apply to MCP requests (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/mcp-server).
The deprecated `force user password generate` and `force user permset(license) assign` commands are removed on 2027-03-01 (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Data Cloud became Data 360 (https://www.salesforce.com/data/).
Agent Script topics became subagents in April 2026 (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Heroku Integration became Heroku AppLink (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-applink).
`sf org open authoring-bundle` became `sf org open agent --authoring-bundle` (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Agentforce for Developers became Agentforce Vibes (date unverified) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).
Einstein Copilot became Agentforce (2024, unverified here) (https://github.com/forcedotcom/cli/blob/main/releasenotes/README.md).

Unconfirmed: because developer.salesforce.com returned HTTP 403 and search budget ran out, the hosted MCP GA date (2026-04-29), editions and Flex Credits billing come from search-result extracts and secondary guides, and server tool lists and the sandbox URL pattern come from secondary guides (open question in the note).

Unconfirmed: an official Agentforce limits page (agents per org, subagents per agent, actions per subagent, action timeout) could not be read because help.salesforce.com renders through JavaScript, so the 20/15/15 figures are secondary (open question in the note).

Unconfirmed: the official GA date for the Agentforce native MCP client (external MCP servers via Agentforce Registry), A2A support status and the Winter '27 third-party orchestration feature were not confirmed (open question in the note).
